sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: The canonical factor audit retains two or more material facts, counterevidence, confidence and linked evidence for each of 13 factors. Scores: GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 7, CASH 3, BAL 6, EXEC 6, EARN 7, R 2, D 3, P 4, L NS. Exact BQS contributions 1.00+.80+.96+.60+.84+.30+.48+.48=5.46. GQS 3.20+1.20+1.05+1.05+.30=6.80, capped 5.00 because persistent poor conversion scores CASH 3. IAS known contribution is 0.25×5.46+.35×2+.20×3+.10×4=3.065 with 90% coverage; missing L gives [3.165,4.065], not a confidence interval. BQS/GQS may be compared on conditional financial evidence, but IAS is excluded from investment ranking. Moving uncertain GOV and CAP together ±1 moves BQS±.32; GQS raw±.15 and remains capped 5. No value penalty is smuggled into BQS, no GQS premium added to IAS and no missing-factor reweighting occurs.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Kwick selects, sources, configures and integrates forensic kits, mobile forensic vehicles, cyber/digital forensic systems and DNA-related solutions, with installation, training and support. FY26 goods are roughly 91% of sales; equipment rental contributes ₹9.2541 cr and AMC just ₹0.1787 cr. This is substantially a goods/tender business, not 90% subscription software. Supply partners include overseas OEMs; relationships are nonexclusive or deal-specific and Kwick bears integration, client acceptance, warranty and working-capital risk. Laboratory infrastructure is proof-of-concept and demonstration, not a separately valued commercial sample-processing operation. Mobile units 21/47/25 in FY24 / FY25 / FY26 and blended sales per unit approximately ₹20.06/34.91/42.27 lakh illustrate scope, not comparable unit margins: mid FY25 vehicle procurement moved to local dealers and product specifications differ. FY24 KPI revenue ₹4.2137 cr versus segment ₹4.0509 cr remains a small disclosed inconsistency. There is no published contract-level gross margin, acquisition cost, renewal cohort or utilization denominator from which to invent unit economics.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Tender qualification, installation experience, trained staff and supplier relationships create useful execution advantages. Yet supplier 40.86% and top 10 customer 77.64% concentration, nonexclusive OEM access and tiny AMC revenues limit evidence of switching costs or independent intellectual-property rents. Increasing cyber mix reduced the direct-cost gross-margin proxy, consistent with distribution/integration economics rather than widening pricing power. Domestic scientific-instrument maker Holmarc FY25 revenue ₹37.1672 cr grew 11.07%, PAT ₹3.7351 cr grew 8.80%; its manufacturing profile and diluted EPS decline despite profit growth show why revenue labels alone are not comparable. Cellebrite’s Q4 FY25 gross margin 84.7%, subscription share 90% and FY25 ARR$480.8 m/NRR 116% describe a fundamentally different software platform. Thermo Fisher’s FY25 Life Sciences US$10.374 bn segment and 36.3% margin are supplier-scale context, not Kwick targets. No peer multiples are fabricated or directly transferred across these economic differences. MOAT 4 reflects contestability, not denial of operating competence.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Revenue rises from FY21 ₹11.6073 cr to FY26 ₹105.7128 cr, five-year CAGR 55.55%; FY22 ₹3.9579 cr is shown as a genuine trough but not chosen as the favorable scoring base. FY23–FY26 restated three-year CAGR 73.10% corroborates strong expansion. FY24 / FY25 / FY26 additions ₹9.8023/34.8436/40.6859 cr show growing absolute scale, not just percentages. FY26 growth 62.57% is broad in cyber ₹35.2283 cr and forensic ₹39.1084 cr, whereas mobile revenue falls from ₹16.4066 cr to ₹10.5676 cr and units 47 to 25. Government share falls to 55.22% from 78.91%, providing genuine customer-mix change. Five-year original-versus-restated classifications, gross goods pass-through and changed vehicle scope prevent a clean physical-volume CAGR; there is enough segment and customer evidence to score business expansion, not enough to call every rupee proprietary value-added. REV rubric starts 9 above 30%; Medium confidence caps 8 with no separate small-base deduction. Public funds and forecast growth are excluded from REV.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: NFIES ₹2,254.43 cr over FY24–29 is real budgeted demand context, but campuses/civil works and government labs are not entirely contestable Kwick equipment spend. Reported July 2026 order book~ ₹20 cr versus~ ₹39 cr in June 2025 and six-month execution language provide finite, declining snapshot visibility, not a recurring contracted growth annuity. NFSU Varanasi’s ₹150 cr campus announcement expressly disclaims a Kwick award. Aggregate organic incremental economics support CAP 7: FY24–FY26 ΔNOPAT ₹9.955294 cr/ΔIC ₹14.9983 cr=66.38%; adding government receivables/advance tax to the capital increment lowers to 52.46%, still above 16–20% capital cost. Reconciliation: cash capex 3.8268−DA 0.8467+ΔONWC12.0603−book/cash residual 0.0421=ΔIC14.9983. All capitalized RPT software and operating deposits remain in capital. This is a valid same-perimeter multiyear substitute, not a project IRR or current ROCE shortcut; two high-growth increments and mix shifts cap confidence. Cash realization remains poor enough to cap GQS 5 even with strong revenue and profit expansion.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Promoter/group expected post-offer ownership 64.65% retains control; IPO contains both fresh shares and a ₹9.72 cr OFS, which does not fund the company. Main-object noncompliance over 2015–2025 was amended April 2025, adjudicated June 2026 and penalties paid July 2026; do not present the cured issue as unresolved fraud. FY26 statutory audit flags ₹26.07 lakh individual MD remuneration excess. Management explains total MD/WTD pay within 10% profit but individual 5% limit and seeks special ratification; actual passage remains unverified. FY26 managerial remuneration ₹2.8135 cr, software purchases from Gostocks ₹0.20 cr after ₹0.5870 cr FY25, rent and trading RPTs require annual review; related-party debt balances were repaid, and no abusive transfer is established merely by a related-party label. Scaling revenue and adapting mobile procurement support execution, but no full order win/cancel/delivery/collection cohort or promised-capex scorecard is available. Price-query responses deny missing price-sensitive disclosure; they are not an endorsement of valuation. GOV 5/EXEC 6 reflect adequate but imperfect evidence.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: Full FY26 main audit, separate IFC and CARO annexures were inspected, not just the headline opinion. Main/IFC are unmodified; audit trail operated throughout and preserved; bank monthly statements agree books; no reported fraud/default; disputed GST ₹6.28 lakh remains contingent. FY25 package also reports clean IFC/audit trail. FY24 contradictory audit-trail applicability wording is retained with later affirmative counterevidence, not forced into a perpetual G2 Hold. Final FY24 PAT restates ₹2.8716 cr− gratuity 0.0493+deferred tax 0.0124= ₹2.8347 cr; FY25/26 PAT unchanged. Three-year CFO/PAT 38.83%, after financing-classified cash interest 27.42%; cumulative CFO minus capex ₹5.3462 cr is positive but weak relative to profit. FY26 cash ₹13.1632 cr coexists with receivables ₹22.8807 cr, inventory ₹10.4371 cr and payables ₹8.7056 cr. Contract assets not separately disclosed are unknown, not assumed additional cash. CRISIL’s rounded FY25 PAT ₹7.84 cr differs audited ₹8.5594 cr by ₹0.7194 cr; private-placement expense ₹0.7222 cr is near but a causal bridge is unverified, so primary audited PAT governs. All operating rent stays in margins; no lease-debt fiction or one-off addback inflates earnings.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: At ₹200.25/current 21.43644 million shares, equity value ₹429.2647 cr; FY26 earnings on current shares ₹6.3013, P/E 31.78×, post-net-IPO proforma book ₹77.4752 cr and P/B 5.54×. Reserve-adjusted EV/operating EBITDA is 22.19× and EV/sales 3.98× using only cash beyond protection; FY26 CFO minus capex yield is 1.12%. These are dated analytic ratios, not live prices. Entry cash 13.1632+41.0544−4.9859+.4152−13= ₹36.6469 cr; March prepaid fees addback avoids paying them twice. Of ₹31.42 cr WC proceeds, ₹3 cr assumed deployed leaves ₹28.42 cr earmarked. The ₹7.5 cr operating-WC cash reserve overlaps eligible WC earmark, so combined protection=max(earmark, floor), not free money. Tax 4.7002+gratuity 0.5054+capex 1.4103+ONWC 4.1571+other 2.227= ₹13 cr; other pays statutory 1.8303+interest 0.0106+buffer 0.3861. These separately removed claims are not paid again through ONWC. The objects narrative mislabels gross and net proceeds in two sentences; the detailed table and share-count × offer-price arithmetic resolve this, and govern the model. No forecast borrowing is assumed. Exact dated six-stub models retain all cash, tax, capital and protections. Base 17.5% EBITDA, 28% ONWC, 2.5% capex, 12× exit returns 7.04%; entry ₹139.92 meets 15%, and ₹159.69/ ₹123.01 meets 12%/18%. Required constant growth for 15% is 25.57%; DCF ₹55.18– ₹77.44 underscores terminal-multiple dependence. No operating property or demonstration lab is added again.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Permanent impairment is High at this reference price: tender slowdown and customer acceptance delays can coincide with supplier funding, lower gross margins and guarantee calls. Bear FY27 revenue−23.59% models loss of largest-customer-sized revenue, not an accusation that the customer has left; margin 10%, ONWC 48%, exit 7× and ₹5.9285 cr guarantees plus GST produce terminal ₹45.81, -77.12% price change and −25.55% annual return. This bear remains funded under the earmark rules, but combined worse collections/margins and extra pre-entry cash use breaches protected cash. Additional ₹10 cr non-WC pre-entry uses cannot legally consume earmarked proceeds: ordinary/conditional IRRs and entry prices are null in that stress even if algebraic long-run cash later recovers. Severe negative notional cash is not renamed debt. Separate rescue cases explicitly issue whole shares at 60% of reference price with 5% fees and calculate share expansion separately from holder dilution; financing is not claimed available. Recovery depends on collectible contracts and remaining cash, not a high replacement-value narrative.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: A 5× wealth outcome from ₹200.25 in five years requires 37.97% annual return; 10× requires 58.49%. Under base 17.5% EBITDA/28% ONWC/12× exit and unchanged shares, the funded 5× crossing needs 49.90% constant revenue growth and terminal revenue ₹1,020.60 cr, roughly 9.65× FY26 scale. That is algebraically feasible given assumed capital turns but not established by a ₹20 cr order book, nonexclusive suppliers or current execution resources. The 10× search finds no funded crossing in 0–80% constant growth, and correctly reports null rather than a search endpoint. Holding capital intensity constant at such scale is especially optimistic; a collection deterioration invalidates funding. The recent historical high CAGR is a useful contrary fact, not proof that tender economics repeat indefinitely. No premium platform multiple, lab value, undeployed IPO cash double-count or probability-weighted IRR makes these outcomes an investment thesis. Strong commercialization, contract-level margins, collections and share-count discipline would be required before revisiting.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: On the next half-year/annual filing, reconcile bank cash, IPO deployment, current tax/statutory payments, supplier credit and receivable ageing against the ₹13 cr pre-entry envelope; any excess non-WC uses that invade earmark suspend ordinary return interpretation. Quarterly/half-year tender tracking should separate wins, cancellations, delivered goods, accepted goods, invoices and collections, with product-level gross profit and recurring AMC renewals. Require evidence before assigning any NFSU contract or commercial lab revenue. Compare cyber gross margin and goods/service classification to the last disclosed mix. Track guarantees and litigation without treating their face value as certain losses. Obtain the actual remuneration-ratification voting result and future Section 197 compliance, related-party software utility and arm’s-length procurement. Verify auditor/IFC/CARO/audit-trail continuity, not just audit opinion. For G4, obtain BSE traded value, zero-print days, spreads, circuits and current lot/restrictions over 20 and 60 sessions when available; distinguish inaccessible history from zero turnover. Update valuation when actual growth, margins, capital intensity, dilution or funding materially differ. No mechanical buy/sell trigger is prescribed.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Classification: Hold — unresolved for implementation, with a weak setup/value-trap-risk economic matrix under every possible L score. BQS 5.46 is mixed quality; GQS 5 after persistent cash-conversion cap does not qualify as an evidence-backed compounder. This is not Avoid — governance and not a distressed/default label. Financial reliability remains usable conditional on disclosed limitations and full later clean audit evidence; current funding is supported as a conservative analytical envelope, not a verified bank balance. Research-watchlist status means seek collection and deployment evidence, not wait blindly for a lower share price. A lower price cannot repair governance, unit-economics or tradability evidence; a headline order cannot repair cash conversion until collection. IAS remains NS and is not ranked as its midpoint. The user supplied no holding cost, portfolio weight, taxes or risk capacity, so this record makes no personalized allocation or exit-count assertion. No financial transaction is proposed or executed.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary final prospectus, FY21–FY26 statutory reports, company DRHP, full latest audit annexures, issuer presentation/clarifications, CRISIL rationales, MHA reply and named peer issuer reports underpin the evidence. Original PDFs/HTML/OCR are local research sources only; private analytical archives intentionally contain safe financial extracts, URLs and hashes rather than raw documents or personal identifiers. Offline reproduction establishes exact calculations, not fresh external source authenticity. MarketScreener is dated secondary quote evidence; secondary BSE-notice reproduction and official interoperable master together establish identity/lot, while direct BSE file availability was limited. Open material questions: exact post-IPO cash/utilization; remuneration ratification vote; customer/contract unit gross margin and acceptance collections; FY24 mobile KPI reconciliation; separate GST/advance-tax asset composition; supportable 20/60 session execution test. Nonmaterial classification and rating differences are explicitly retained. All scenarios are analyst assumptions; no forecast is a management commitment. No data after 20 October 2026 is incorporated merely because sources were accessed later. Model data are INR crore unless marked per-share, shares or US dollar peer context.

evidence.claim: Performance/bank guarantees ₹5.9285 cr and disputed GST ₹0.0628 cr modeled in bear; they are not actual debt/default. RPT software purchases ₹0.5870 cr FY25 and ₹0.20 cr FY26 are retained in capital; FY26 total managerial remuneration ₹2.8135 cr disclosed.
evidence.locator: Contingent liabilities printed p 244 and related-party Annexure VIII pp 250–254; CARO disputed GST

evidence.claim: FY24–26 aggregate incremental NOPAT ₹9.955294 cr against ΔIC ₹14.9983 cr gives 66.38%; including government balance increase lowers proxy to 52.46%. Stable standalone organic perimeter supports CAP substitute, not contract IRR.
evidence.locator: Restated financials; model incremental_return_bridge

evidence.claim: ₹13 cr pre-entry uses reserve known tax/gratuity/statutory/interest plus half-year capex, ONWC and buffer 0. Opening cash ₹36.6469 cr less remaining WC earmark ₹28.42 cr leaves ₹8.2269 cr unrestricted. This is a conservative analytical bridge, not an observed October balance.
evidence.locator: Model opening_cash_bridge and financial_inputs funding_assumptions

evidence.claim: 19 October delayed secondary close ₹200.25; four observations only. No 60-session BSE traded-value/spread/circuit history retrieved. NSE absence is missing coverage, not zero volume.
evidence.locator: Dated price rows; exact issuer master

evidence.claim: Holmarc FY25 revenue ₹37.1672 cr,+11.07%, PAT ₹3.7351 cr,+8.80%, EPS ₹3.72 versus ₹3.94 due share denominator. Scientific-instrument manufacturing differs from Kwick integration.
evidence.locator: Annual report pp 46 and 89

evidence.claim: Cellebrite Q4 FY25 subscription share 90%, gross margin 84.7%, FY25 ARR$480.8 m/NRR 116%; it is not a like-for-like multiple peer. Thermo Fisher Life Sciences FY25$10.374 bn with 36.3% segment margin is a supplier-scale contrast.
evidence.locator: Cellebrite Q4 release; Thermo segment results

evidence.claim: Base 17.5% EBITDA, tapering 18%→14% growth, 28% ONWC and 12× exit produces below 15% hurdle; bear and bull not assigned probabilities. DCF independently tests 16–20% discount and 3–5% terminalgrowth.
evidence.locator: Full dated model including every annual row

evidence.claim: Preoffer 16,874,840 to post 21,436,440 shares expands denominator 27.03% and dilutes prior holder ownership 21.28%; FY26 ₹8 historical EPS becomes ₹6.30 on current denominator before returns on new cash.
evidence.locator: Capital structure and EPS note

evidence.claim: Direct-cost gross-margin proxy fell roughly 37%→31%→27% as cyber product mix grew, while operating EBITDA excluding other income remained 17.78/18.76/17.95%. Profit growth is operating-led but not evidence of expanding pricing power.
evidence.locator: Restated cost notes and business mix

evidence.claim: No subsidiaries/JVs/associates; related-party loans nil March 2026, total borrowing repaid. Fresh issue is not a rescue assumed prospectively: issued shares are already reflected in the dated official master.
evidence.locator: Corporate group/borrowings and capital master

evidence.claim: CRISIL FY25 PAT ₹7.84 cr versus audited ₹8.5594 cr differs ₹0.7194 cr (rounded rating); private placement cost ₹0.7222 cr is near but not an explicitly verified causal bridge. Primary audited figures govern.
evidence.locator: CRISIL key financial indicators; prospectus issue-expense reserve movement

evidence.claim: Objects narrative mislabels gross/net proceeds in two sentences, but the explicit table reconciles fresh 4,561,600× ₹90= ₹41.0544 cr, less companyexpenses ₹4.9859 cr=net ₹36.0685 cr. Model uses share-price arithmetic and detailedtable, not inconsistent prose.
evidence.locator: Printed pp 87–88 and capital structure

normalization.cfo_interest: Financing classification. Show both reported CFO and after-finance-cash conversion.
normalization.cash_capex: Tangible + intangible + development cash additions; excludes interest receipts, asset sales and advances.
normalization.ic: Equity + debt + gratuity + current tax liability + statutory dues + accrued interest minus cash, deferred tax asset, government balances and prepaid IPO costs. This equals net operating assets with all capitalized software and operating security deposits; no double valuation of operating real estate.
normalization.government_balances: Mixed GST/advance-tax balance not separately disclosed; excluded in core IC, included in alternate conservative denominator.
normalization.history_comparability: FY21–22 original context; FY23 DRHP restated; FY24–26 final restated. Revenue recasting under 0.4% at endpoints does not explain growth. Original FY22 pandemic-depressed year not selected for CAGR.

funding_assumptions.status: Analyst conservative sources-and-uses bridge, not an observed October bank balance. No borrowing, optional warrant proceeds, IPO receivable or hypothetical refinancing assumed.

valuation.quote_status: Dated secondary delayed BSE close 19 October 2026; not executable quote
valuation.funding_basis: March audited cash plus completed fresh issuance evidenced by current listed share count and final offer terms; full fees netted, OFS excluded, known claims and conservative pre-entry uses reserved. Conservative stress is support, not proof of actual October cash. No renewed bank limit assumed.

incremental_return_bridge.limitation: Organic aggregate proxy, not contract-level IRR. Captures capex, working capital, deposits and software. Cash-to-book fixed residual is separately retained, not assumed zero. Product mix shifted; one-year ratio is not sole evidence. Cost-of-capital range 16–20%.
